entries.title: What to know as Trump visits Xi in China
entries.snippet: Trump has landed in Beijing for the first visit by a US leader since his own in 2017.

entries.title: More than 1,000 passengers held on cruise after gastrointestinal illness outbreak
entries.snippet: The ship, which set sail from Belfast on Friday, is at port in Bordeaux after 49 people fell ill from gastrointestinal illness.

entries.title: Climbers clear path to Everest summit past giant chunk of ice
entries.snippet: Nearly 1,000 climbers will attempt to scale the peak in coming weeks and this has raised safety concerns.

entries.title: Shrinking Milka chocolate bar tricked consumers, says German court
entries.snippet: A court in Bremen has found the manufacturer of the classic Alpine Milk chocolate bar guilty of "shrinkflation".

entries.title: Gaza sisters win prize for turning rubble into reusable bricks
entries.snippet: Displaced teenagers Farah and Tala wanted to 'turn destruction into something useful'.

entries.title: Nigerian film star Alexx Ekubo dies aged 40
entries.snippet: The actor was recognised for his contributions to entertainment as well as his humanitarian efforts.

entries.title: Thousands of Waymos recalled after robotaxi swept into a creek
entries.snippet: The voluntary recall follows an incident on 20 April where an empty Waymo car entered a flooded road in San Antonio, Texas.

entries.title: Ghana to evacuate 300 from South Africa over anti-immigrant protests
entries.snippet: The foreign minister says the "distressed" Ghanaians registered with the embassy in Pretoria to be evacuated.

entries.title: Air India crisis deepens ahead of final Ahmedabad crash report
entries.snippet: Air India faces a leadership vacuum and mounting financial losses as it struggles to recover from the crash.

entries.title: Jason Collins, NBA's first openly gay player, dies aged 47
entries.snippet: Collins shared late last year that he had been diagnosed with an aggressive form of brain cancer.

entries.title: Trump's 'Golden Dome' will cost $1.2tn and might not stop all-out missile attack
entries.snippet: That pricetag is nearly seven times higher than Trump's initial estimate, found an independent budget office.

entries.title: Lebanon says two paramedics among 13 killed in Israeli strikes
entries.snippet: Lebanon's health ministry says the paramedics were carrying out a rescue mission in Nabatieh in response to an earlier attack that killed one person.

entries.title: Zelensky's ex-chief of staff in court as Ukraine corruption probe escalates
entries.snippet: Andriy Yermak was named by Ukraine's two anti-corruption agencies as a suspect in a money-laundering scheme.

entries.title: Thief jailed after stealing unreleased Beyoncé music from car
entries.snippet: The man smashed into a car and stole luggage containing hard drives with the singer's tracks.

entries.title: No sign of larger hantavirus outbreak, says UN health agency
entries.snippet: The situation could still change and there might be more confirmed cases, warns the head of the World Health Organization.

entries.title: Hamas 'weaponised' sexual violence in 7 October attacks, Israeli investigation says
entries.snippet: The most comprehensive report of its kind details harrowing cases of sexual attacks which it says were systematic.

entries.title: Dali ship operator charged over deadly Baltimore bridge collapse
entries.snippet: Six construction workers were killed and several vehicles plunged into the river after the cargo ship crashed into the bridge.

entries.title: eBay rejects $55.5bn offer from GameStop
entries.snippet: The online auction giant said it doubted how the video game retailer would finance its offer.

entries.title: Uganda's president sworn in for record seventh term
entries.snippet: Yoweri Museveni, 81, won disputed elections in January to extend his 40-year rule.

entries.title: South Africa's top court bars repeat asylum applications
entries.snippet: The home affairs minister hails the ruling as a "victory" against the "abuse" of the refugee system.

entries.title: War in Iran costs $29 billion so far. And, students are finally improving in math
entries.snippet: Pentagon officials told Congress they estimate the war in Iran has cost $29 billion so far. And, a new Education Scorecard shows U.S. students are improving in math.

entries.title: Putin hails Russia's test launch of a new ballistic missile
entries.snippet: Russia test-fired a new intercontinental ballistic missile as part of efforts to modernize its nuclear forces. The nuclear-armed Sarmat missile would enter combat service at the end of the year.

entries.title: Japanese snack packages turning black-and-white as Iran war depletes ink supply
entries.snippet: The packaging on some snacks is turning black-and-white, as the war in Iran disrupts the supply of an ingredient used in colored ink. Calbee's chips originally came in a bright-orange bag.

entries.title: Some Minneapolis donors have moved on. The immigrants waiting for help haven't
entries.snippet: During Operation Metro Surge, mutual aid efforts raised millions of dollars. But with most agents gone and increasing fatigue from the community, funds are drying up and people are moving on. Immigrants are not.

entries.title: An intimate look at one military family's life on pause as the Iran war continues
entries.snippet: Military life has always involved some degree of uncertainty. But for many families, the fear and unknowns that come with the Iran war are new territory.

entries.title: How the Trump administration has undermined the fight against public corruption
entries.snippet: At least 15 former elected officials and co-conspirators with corruption offenses have been pardoned by President Trump in the last year, undermining the fight against public corruption.

entries.title: Short flights are popular. Will they last?
entries.snippet: Some flights are less than 100 miles, and they're the backbone of the U.S. air system, linking small towns and big cities. But short routes were in decline even before jet fuel costs spiked.

entries.title: Is the U.S. slipping into 'Competitive Authoritarianism?'
entries.snippet: What form of government do we have in America now? Some scholars say it is no longer liberal democracy, but "competitive authoritarianism." NPR's Frank Langfitt explains the term and its origin.

entries.title: French hantavirus patient is critically ill as outbreak grows to 11
entries.snippet: A French woman infected in the deadly hantavirus outbreak on a cruise ship is critically ill and being treated with an artificial lung. The outbreak has now reached 11 total reported cases, 9 of which have been confirmed.

entries.title: $4.8M settlement reached over Louisiana traffic stop death, AP sources say
entries.snippet: Louisiana officials have agreed to a tentative $4.8 million settlement with the family of Ronald Greene, a Black motorist who died during a violent roadside arrest carried out by five white officers.

entries.title: Hegseth grilled over direction of Iran war and costs for Americans
entries.snippet: Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth testified in back-to-back Capitol Hill hearings where he faced bipartisan frustration about the Iran war and its rising costs. With neither the Americans nor the Iranians softening their demands, the President left for a high-stakes visit to Iran's

entries.title: Inflation could hit 4% next month and stay elevated for rest of year, economist warns
entries.snippet: The latest inflation report shows price increases for American consumers in April hit a three-year high, driven by a spike in the cost of gasoline. The Consumer Price Index, which includes energy and food costs, rose 3.8% year-over-year, according to the Labor Department. Geoff B

entries.title: What's at stake as Trump heads to China for talks with Xi
entries.snippet: President Trump is traveling halfway around the world for a state visit to China, and he's bringing a host of top American executives with him. Talks there are expected to encompass the complex economic and security postures of both nations. Nick Schifrin reports from Beijing.

entries.title: News Wrap: FDA head Marty Makary resigning after uneven tenure

entries.title: Louisiana's redistricting rush ignites debate over race and representation
entries.snippet: With its House primary contests off the calendar for now, Louisiana is taking another step to redraw its political battle lines. The move comes after the Supreme Court once again pared back landmark civil rights protections. Once the lines are settled in Louisiana, the impacts wi

entries.title: Israeli lawmakers set up a special tribunal and allow for death penalty for Hamas-led 2023 attackers
entries.snippet: Rights groups have criticized the measure, saying it makes the death penalty too easy to impose while also doing away with procedures safeguarding the right to a fair trial.

entries.title: Inside Izyum, the Ukrainian frontline city facing the threat of a 2nd Russian occupation
entries.snippet: As Russia prepares for a large-scale spring offensive, a city near the frontline is preparing for the worst. Control of Izyum is vital for Ukraine as the link between Kharkiv and Donetsk. Izyum was occupied by Russian forces for six months in 2022. Ukrainian forces liberated it a

entries.title: Students question value of college as costs rise and AI reshapes jobs
entries.snippet: This season's college commencement celebrations come at a sobering moment. Students are facing steep loans and dicey job prospects, especially in the AI era. That's led many to question whether a college degree is worth it anymore. Paul Solman visited Michigan to find out how som

entries.title: Helen Zoe Veit and Amna Nawaz discuss picky eaters on 'Settle In'
entries.snippet: How did American kids become such picky eaters? On our Settle In podcast, Amna Nawaz asked that question to author and historian Helen Zoe Veit. Her latest book is "Picky: How American Children Became the Fussiest Eaters in History."

entries.title: Conan O'Brien will return to host the 99th Academy Awards next year
entries.snippet: Despite a dip in viewership this year, social media engagement rose significantly.

entries.title: U.K. Prime Minister Starmer defiant as calls for his resignation grow
entries.snippet: While more than 100 Labour lawmakers signed a letter of support for Starmer, about 90 others urged him to set a timetable for his departure.

entries.title: WATCH: 'I don't think about Americans' financial situation' when negotiating with Iran, Trump says
entries.snippet: A reporter asked Trump on Tuesday to what extent Americans' financial straits are motivating him to make a deal.

entries.title: Trump's redistricting push falters in South Carolina Senate but notches a win in Missouri's top court
entries.snippet: South Carolina senators defied his push Tuesday, while Missouri's top court upheld a new map backed by Trump that could benefit Republicans in the midterm elections.

entries.title: WATCH: Murray calls Pentagon's Iran war cost estimate 'suspiciously low,' presses for damage price tag
entries.snippet: Jules Hurst, the Pentagon comptroller, told members of Congress at an earlier hearing before a House Appropriations panel, that the cost of the war had risen to $29 billion.

entries.title: Push for South Carolina to join congressional redistricting battle fails as Republicans reject map
entries.snippet: The 29-17 vote failed, with just two votes short of the two-thirds needed.

entries.title: WATCH: FBI Director Kash Patel, ATF, DEA heads testify in Senate hearing
entries.snippet: FBI Director Kash Patel angrily lashed out at a Democratic lawmaker at a budget hearing Tuesday, calling allegations that he drinks excessively on the job and has been unreachable at times to his staff "unequivocally, categorically false."

entries.title: Appeals court says Trump doesn't have to pay $83 million to E. Jean Carroll — for now
entries.snippet: The 2nd U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals has agreed to let Trump delay the payment to E. Jean Carroll as long as he posts a $7.4 million bond to cover interest that would accrue through October.

entries.title: Supreme Court halts order on Alabama's U.S. House map, giving GOP an opening to gain seat
entries.snippet: The U.S. Supreme Court on Monday set the stage for Alabama to eliminate one of two largely Black congressional districts before this year's midterm elections.

entries.title: Ship operators fear fuel shortages as Iran war squeezes supply
entries.snippet: Experts say consumers and companies should brace for price spikes to shipping costs and impacts to bottom lines.

entries.title: Memphis Grizzlies forward Brandon Clarke dies at 29
entries.snippet: Memphis Grizzlies forward Brandon Clarke has died, according to the team, his agency and the NBA.

entries.title: DW
entries.snippet: News, Analysis and Service from Germany and Europe - in 30 Languages

entries.title: Gunshots heard at Philippine Senate as ICC arrest expected
entries.snippet: Gunshots have been reported inside the Philippine Senate as armed troops entered the building. The chaos comes as one senator faces imminent arrest over an ICC warrant.

entries.title: Trump arrives in China ahead of summit with Xi Jinping
entries.snippet: President Donald Trump is expected to address the Iran war, trade and Taiwan in talks with China's Xi Jinping. DW has more.

entries.title: Fake TikTok fans and the history of 'unethical' music marketing
entries.snippet: Do indie darlings like Sombr and Geese owe their success to TikTok "trend simulations"? The question has sent shockwaves through their fan base. Yet manipulated charts are as old as the music business itself.

entries.title: Cem Özdemir, first German state premier with Turkish roots
entries.snippet: Cem Özdemir is the first leader of a German federal state to have Turkish roots. His Green Party won elections in the wealthy southwestern region of Baden-Württemberg.

entries.title: Ceasefire in sight? What's next for Russia's war in Ukraine
entries.snippet: Four years since Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine, is the end finally in sight? DW spoke to US political experts about why they think US home elections could bring about a ceasefire.

entries.title: Iran war: Oil stocks being used up at record pace, IEA warns
entries.snippet: The International Energy Agency warned of "rapidly shrinking buffers." Meanwhile, Iranian Foreign Minister Araghchi is en route to Delhi for a BRICS gathering which is set to be dominated by the conflict. DW has more.

entries.title: Germany news: Carmakers paint bleak picture on jobs
entries.snippet: German automakers say there is a strong likelihood of huge job losses over the next decade. Meanwhile, Germany's football fans are wondering whether former national keeper Manuel Neuer is set to return. DW has more.

entries.title: China’s new rules give the West a new headache
entries.snippet: Beijing now has strong new powers to punish firms for pulling manufacturing out of China. Multinationals are increasingly caught in a web of coercion and complex rules as they try to operate across the US, EU and China.

entries.title: Satellites add a new layer to global poverty data
entries.snippet: A new study using satellite data finds that 58% of the global population has been assigned to the wrong tier in the UN's Human Development Index. That can have real-world consequences for how aid reaches people.

entries.title: India's Modi cuts size of convoy in austerity move — reports
entries.snippet: Prime Minister Narendra Modi has reportedly reduced the number of vehicles in his official convoy. The reports come as Modi is making an austerity appeal to Indians. DW has the latest.

entries.title: Is caring about the climate unmanly?
entries.snippet: The answer is complex — and says a lot about how masculinity works in the modern world.

entries.title: Nauru moves to change its name in break from colonial past
entries.snippet: The parliament of Nauru has agreed to change the South Pacific microstate's name to "Naoero". A referendum will now take place on the constitutional change.

entries.title: Argentina sees vast protests against Milei's university cuts
entries.snippet: Organizers estimated that some 600,000 students, university staff, union members and opposition supporters attended the protest in Buenos Aires alone.

entries.title: OpenAI boss Sam Altman says Musk wanted control of company
entries.snippet: Sam Altman testified in trial that could determine the future of OpenAI, the company behind ChatGPT.

entries.title: Canvas owner secures student data in deal with hacking group
entries.snippet: The ShinyHunters hacking group stole student data from the popular education platform Canvas last week. Parent company Instructure apologized for the hack and said Canvas "remains safe to use."

entries.title: Iran: Surge of political prisoners amid US-Israel war
entries.snippet: Amid the US-Israel war with Iran, as the world breathlessly watches the Strait of Hormuz, Tehran is quietly increasing pressure on political prisoners. Advocates are sounding the alarm, warning of mass executions.

entries.title: EU invites Taliban members to discuss Afghan migrant returns
entries.snippet: The European Commission has invited officials from Afghanistan's Taliban to discuss the returns of certain migrants. It's controversial on humanitarian grounds, and because Brussels doesn't recognize Taliban authority.

entries.title: War in Iran: Despite Iranian attacks, Doha steps up mediation efforts
entries.snippet: Qatar is intensifying regional mediation efforts despite the Iran war bringing airstrikes and cutting off Doha's access to global oil markets. But can Qatar leverage its ties to the US and Iran for its own benefit?

entries.title: Hotter 2026 and El Nino could trigger extreme fires
entries.snippet: More than 150 million hectares — over twice the size of Texas — burned globally in the first months of 2026. With a high chance of a supercharged El Nino, the second half of the year could be even worse.
